texts.error.no_memory_for_the_engine_s_stack: There is no memory for the engine's stack.
texts.error.out_of_memory_for_the_picture: There is not enough memory for the picture.
texts.firmware.characters_pk3.about: Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, Amy, Fang and Metal Sonic. The game checks the file's MD5 checksum itself.
texts.firmware.music_pk3.about: The game's music: the Ogg Vorbis songs, and the MIDI songs that the Music Preference setting can play.
texts.firmware.srb2_pk3.about: The game's graphics, sounds, objects and scripts. The game checks the file's MD5 checksum itself.
texts.firmware.zones_pk3.about: The game's levels. The game checks the file's MD5 checksum itself.
texts.property.boss_active: Whether a boss is in the level. The boss is the first object with the MF_BOSS flag in the game's list of objects, found the same way the SRB2 TAS build finds it. When there is none, the other Boss values are 0.
texts.property.boss_flashing: Whether the boss is flashing after a hit (MF2_FRET). It cannot be hit again until it stops.
texts.property.boss_health: The boss's health: the hits it has left.
texts.property.boss_max_health: The boss's health at the start (the spawnhealth of its object type).
texts.property.game_map: The number of the current map (gamemap).
texts.property.game_state: The game's state (gamestate). 1 means a level is being played.
texts.property.game_tic: The game's tic counter (gametic). A tic is 1/35 of a second.
texts.property.player_angle: The direction the player's object faces. 2^32 is a full turn, 0 is east, and it grows counterclockwise.
texts.property.player_charging_spindash: Whether a spindash is being charged (PF_STARTDASH, one bit of Player.Flags).
texts.property.player_conveyor_momentum_x: What a conveyor or a moving platform carrying the player adds to Momentum X (player->cmomx), in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_conveyor_momentum_y: What a conveyor or a moving platform carrying the player adds to Momentum Y (player->cmomy), in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_dash_speed: The charge of the spindash (player->dashspeed), which is the speed it launches at. It starts at Min Dash and grows by 1.0 for each tic Spin is held, up to Max Dash. In 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_dashmode: Metal Sonic's dash mode counter (player->dashmode): the tics spent at running speed. Dash mode starts at 105 (DASHMODE_THRESHOLD), and the count stops at 108 (DASHMODE_MAX).
texts.property.player_flags: The player's flags (player->pflags, the PF_* values in SRB2's source code).
texts.property.player_in_level: Whether the player has an object in a level. When not, the other Player and Timers values are 0.
texts.property.player_max_dash: The largest spindash charge of the character (player->maxdash), in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_min_dash: The smallest spindash charge of the character (player->mindash), in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_momentum_x: The player's movement in map units per tic, in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_normal_speed: The player's top running speed (player->normalspeed). Dash mode raises it. In 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_platform_momentum_z: The vertical movement of the moving floor the player stands on (mo->pmomz). It is kept after the player leaves the floor. In 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_speed: The player's horizontal speed as the game calculates it (player->speed), measured against the floor the player stands on, in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_x: The player's position, in 16.16 fixed point: 65536 is one map unit.
texts.property.player_y: The player's position, in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.player_z: The player's height, in 16.16 fixed point.
texts.property.timers_space: Tics of air left in space (pw_spacetime).
texts.setting.autobrake.about: Makes the player slow down on their own when no direction is held, instead of skidding on (SRB2's console variable autobrake).
texts.setting.cameradistance.about: How far behind the player the camera is, in map units (SRB2's console variable cam_dist). The default is SRB2's. It is used by the Manual and Strafe play styles. Automatic and Old Analog use SRB2's simple camera instead, which has its own setting (cam_simpledist).
texts.setting.cameraheight.about: How high above the player the camera is, in map units (SRB2's console variable cam_height). The default is SRB2's. It is used by the Manual and Strafe play styles. Automatic and Old Analog use SRB2's simple camera instead, which has its own setting (cam_simpleheight).
texts.setting.cameraspeed.about: How quickly the camera catches up with the player, from 0 to 1 (SRB2's console variable cam_speed). SRB2's own default is 0.3.
texts.setting.flipcamera.about: Turns the camera upside down when the player's gravity is reversed (SRB2's console variable flipcam).
texts.setting.fov.about: How wide the camera's view is, in degrees across, from 60 to 179 (SRB2's console variable fov). It works in both renderers. The default, 90, is SRB2's. Leave it at 90 for normal levels and set it to 120 for NiGHTS levels, where the wider view shows more of the track ahead. It changes only the picture: the game plays the same at every field of view.
texts.setting.glshaders.about: Turns on the OpenGL renderer's shaders (SRB2's console variable gr_shaders), which give SRB2's lighting, fog and palette look. When it is off, the picture is drawn without shaders, in OpenGL's older fixed way. It changes only the picture: the game is the same either way.
texts.setting.musicpref.about: Which of a song's two versions plays (SRB2's console variable musicpref). Digital: the recorded music (Ogg Vorbis). MIDI: the game's MIDI songs, played on six emulated YM2612 sound chips (the chip of the Sega Genesis / Mega Drive, using MAME's emulation), as SRB2's official Windows builds play them, at SRB2's MIDI volume (midimusicvolume). A song that has only one version plays that one. It changes only the sound: the game plays the same with either.
texts.setting.playstyle.about: The play style of player 1 (Setup > Play Style in SRB2's menu). Strafe: the player always faces the way the camera looks. Manual: the player faces the way it moves, and the camera does not turn by itself. Automatic: the camera turns to follow the player; this is SRB2's own default. Old Analog: the analog control of SRB2 2.1.
texts.setting.renderer.about: Which renderer draws the game. software: SRB2's software renderer. opengl-hw: SRB2's OpenGL renderer, drawn on this computer's graphics card (GPU) through Chimera's GPU bridge. It is fast, but the picture depends on the graphics driver, so Chimera marks a run made with it as not deterministic (not certain to replay exactly the same). If the GPU bridge is not available, the game is drawn in software instead, which plays differently, and the log says so. The renderer is part of the game, because a few things play differently in OpenGL, so a movie must be played back with the renderer it was made with.
texts.setting.resolution.about: The size of the picture, with square pixels. The choices are SRB2's own video modes, plus 2560x1440 and 3840x2160. SRB2's own default is 1280x800. Only the picture changes: the game plays the same at every resolution. A larger picture is slower to draw; turbo (fast forward) skips only the last conversion of the picture, not the drawing.
texts.setting.scoretimerings.about: How the heads-up display (HUD) shows the time (SRB2's console variable timerres). Classic: m:ss. Centiseconds: m:ss.cc. Mania: m:ss.cc, with the score and ring counts lined up under it as in Sonic Mania. Tics: the number of tics (1/35 of a second) spent on the level.
texts.setting.skin.about: The character to play in the Start Map, by its skin name: sonic, tails, knuckles, amy, fang, metalsonic, or one from an add-on (the game's +skin option). Leave it empty for the game's default, Sonic. It is used only together with a Start Map; without one, the character is chosen in the game's character select. A locked character (Amy, Fang, Metal Sonic) also needs Unlock All Characters.
texts.setting.tutorialprompt.about: Whether the title screen asks "Do you want to play a brief Tutorial?" the first time the game starts (SRB2's console variable tutorialprompt). SRB2's own default is on.
texts.setting.unlockall.about: Starts with everything that can be unlocked already unlocked: the modes, the characters, Level Select, Sound Test, Pandora's Box, the emblem hints and radar, and the rest.
texts.setting.unlockcharacters.about: Starts with every character unlocked (Amy, Fang and Metal Sonic).
texts.setting.unlockmaps: Unlock All Maps in Record Attack and NiGHTS Mode
texts.setting.unlockmaps.about: Lets every map that Record Attack and NiGHTS Mode list be chosen, whether it has been visited or not, including the maps of add-ons. Only the menu's check changes; the saved game data is not touched. The modes themselves also need Unlock Record Attack, NiGHTS Mode and Marathon Run.
texts.setting.unlockmodes: Unlock Record Attack, NiGHTS Mode and Marathon Run
texts.setting.unlockmodes.about: Starts with Record Attack and NiGHTS Mode unlocked, so a run does not need a movie that earns them first. SRB2 offers Marathon Run whenever Record Attack is unlocked.
texts.setting.warp.about: The map to start in, written as the game's -warp option takes it (a number, or MAPxx). Leave it empty to start as the game normally does, with the intro and the title screen. SRB2 treats warping to a map not yet visited as a cheat, so the game data (unlocks, emblems and records) is then neither loaded nor saved.
texts.slot.addons.help: Mods, levels and characters (.pk3, .wad, .soc, .lua), in the order they are loaded, as SRB2's -file option loads them. Leave this empty to play the game itself.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The game progress to start from: gamedata.dat (unlocks, emblems and records) and save slots (srb2sav*.ssg), with those file names, as Export Save Data writes them. Leave this empty for a new game.
